title: Health complaints and heat stress prevention strategies during taper as predictors of peaked athletic performance at the 2015 World Athletics Championship in hot conditions
authors: Timpka T, Periard JD, Spreco A, Dahlstrom O, Jacobsson J, Bargoria V, Andersson C, Alonso JM, Racinais S
journal: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport
population: Elite athletes (sprint/power and endurance/combined events) at the 2015 World Athletics Championships in Beijing
findings: 245 of 841 eligible athletes (29%) participated; peaking defined from pre-competition ranking and final competition rank.
Athletes with concern-causing health complaints during the taper were less likely to peak (sprint/power OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.11-0.94; endurance/combined OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.14-1.00).
Endurance/combined athletes who chose pre-cooling were less likely to peak (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.15-0.80).

Sprint/power athletes reporting a sudden-onset injury complaint during the taper displayed increased peaking (OR 4.47, 95% CI 1.28-15.59); authors suggest heat strategies be individually tested before championships.
limitations: Elite track-and-field athletes, 29% response rate, self-report; peaking proxied by rank not time; pre-cooling result likely confounded by choice; not distance-running specific.
implications: Add a taper-phase health check: logged illness, niggles or high concern should prompt an adjustment prompt (rest or reduce) rather than keeping the schedule.
Heat-mitigation strategies should be trialled before race day; no numeric parameter is justified.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (JSAMS Apr 2020); authors list verified, nine authors. Observational.
